final.title: Measure the control, not just the task
final.body:
If you are comparing automation with manual work or another hire, start with one recurring workflow and ask a narrower question: where do your controls actually fail today? For a small business, the useful comparison is not “AI or no AI” in the abstract. It is whether a bounded system can enforce the same approval gates, exception handling, and audit trail you already need, without handing over high-risk decisions. Money movement stays with you. That part is not negotiable.

A practical next step is to pick one repeatable process — invoice review, customer-data entry, or email triage — and map the control points on paper. For each step, note who approves, what gets checked, and what evidence is kept. Then compare that with a simple automation design: can it extract or classify the data, apply the rules, and log exceptions before a human decides? If it cannot, the workflow is probably a bad fit.

That is the real comparison: manual-only control versus controlled automation, with the owner still making the final call. The goal is a workflow you can audit, not a clever shortcut that needs supervision anyway. If the process has no clear paper trail or repeatable approval rule, it is telling you something already.
